h1: The 6 Best Laptop Storage and Charging Carts of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Laptop Charging Carts 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six laptop storage and charging carts, from 16 to 36 device capacity, compared on locks, surge protection and assembly.
summary: The Meteteel 20-device cart is our best overall pick, thanks to independently locking doors and 95 percent pre-assembly. VEVOR is the best 16-device lockable pick, TIOPLY and Plugsharge handle the biggest fleets, and Hupsjer is the lower-cost option.
intro: A charging cart buyer usually counts devices and stops there. The costlier mistakes come later: a cart that ships flat-packed and eats a weekend, or one with no real lock, or a slot too small for the laptops you actually own.
We ranked six carts on capacity, locking, surge protection and assembly, drawing only on listing details. Treat the numbers as listed claims and confirm your device size before ordering.

products.name: Meteteel Fully Assembled 20 Device Laptop Charging Cart for School (Black)
products.verdict: Twenty slots, locking front and back doors, and almost no assembly.
products.description:
The Meteteel 20-device cart has independently locking front and back doors, a ventilated steel frame and built-in cable management. It ships 95 percent pre-assembled and is priced $200-500.

It beats the VEVOR on capacity by four slots while matching it on security basics. The tradeoff is a higher device count than a small classroom may need.

Choose it for a school or office that wants a cart ready within minutes. Check your laptop thickness before buying.
cons: Sized for 20, may be too many
products.skipIf: You only have a handful of devices.

products.name: VEVOR 16 Device Charging Station with Lock & Key, Mobile Charging Cart
products.verdict: A confirmed lock and key, surge protection and 16 slots.
products.description:
The VEVOR holds 16 devices with a confirmed lock and key, built-in surge protection and an integrated power strip. It has two locking casters and is priced $200-500.

It ranks just under the Meteteel because it holds four fewer devices and its listing says nothing about assembly. Its plus is the clearly stated lock and surge combination.

Pick it for a medium-size classroom or team. Half-locking casters mean rolling it needs care.

products.name: TIOPLY 36 Device Charging Cart for Laptop Up to 16.3-inch Screen, Mobile Charging
products.verdict: The largest capacity here, 36 devices, with lock and key doors.
products.description:
The TIOPLY holds 36 devices and laptops up to 16.3 inches. It has lock and key doors, a power-line management bar and a mix of two fixed and two swivel wheels. It is priced $200-500.

It places third because its wheel setup, two fixed and two swivel, is not described as locking. It wins on raw capacity and large-screen support.

Choose it for a large school fleet or big-screen laptops. Roll it with care when fully loaded.

products.name: Plugsharge 32-Device Laptop Charging Cart for Chromebooks, iPad & Tablets
products.verdict: Thirty-two numbered slots with individual cable organizers.
products.description:
The Plugsharge holds 32 devices up to 15.6 inches, with surge and ground fault protection, 32 individual cable organizers and numbered slots. Its open rack design is priced $200-500.

It trails the TIOPLY because the open rack stores devices in view rather than behind locked doors. The numbered slots and cable organizers are its best features.

Pick it for Chromebook and tablet fleets that need order. It is the weaker choice if security is the priority.
cons: Open rack, no door lock listed

products.name: Pearington 30 Device Mobile Charging/Storage Cart for iPads, Tablets, Laptop
products.verdict: Thirty bays plus two bonus outlets, but you assemble it.
products.description:
The Pearington has 30 bays with 13 inch screen slots, cable management in the dividers and 2 bonus outlets, so 32 devices charge while 30 are stored and locked. It requires full assembly and is priced $200-500.

It ranks below the Plugsharge because slots top out at 13 inches and the cart arrives unassembled. Its useful trick is the two extra outlets.

Choose it for tablets and smaller laptops when you are willing to build it. Large laptops will not fit.
products.idealFor: Tablet-heavy fleets with some small laptops.

products.name: Hupsjer 16-Device Mobile Charging Cart, Laptop Charging Station w/Storage Shelf
products.verdict: A 16-device cart with a separate cable and adapter compartment, one tier cheaper.
products.description:
The Hupsjer holds 16 devices and adds a separate cable and adapter compartment measuring 25.2 by 15 by 3.5 inches. It has adjustable removable dividers, a padded shelf and 2 of 4 casters lock. It is priced $100-200.

It ranks last because no lock or surge protection is stated in the facts we have, while cheaper means fewer stated safeguards. The extra compartment is genuinely useful.

Buy it for a small team on a budget. Verify security features before you rely on it.

methodology.description: We compared how many devices each cart stores and charges.

methodology.title: Security
methodology.description: Locking doors or lock and key earned more credit than an open rack.

methodology.title: Power protection
methodology.description: Surge, ground fault and breaker details counted when listed.

methodology.title: Assembly
methodology.description: Pre-assembled carts beat flat-packs for the time they save.

methodology.title: Device size
methodology.description: Maximum screen size decides whether your laptops actually fit.

whatMatters.detail: This is how many laptops or tablets the cart stores and charges at once. It matters because buying too small forces a second cart. Count your devices and add room to grow, then read the capacity in the title.
A lock keeps devices in the cart overnight. Doors with lock and key protect better than an open rack. The listing states whether doors lock and how many.
Surge protection and breakers guard devices charging together. Without them, a power spike can damage several at once. Look for surge or breaker mentions in the specs.
Slots have a maximum screen size, such as 13, 14, 15.6 or 16.3 inches. Laptops that are bigger or thicker will not fit. Compare your laptop size to the listed limit.
Some carts ship nearly assembled and some flat. A flat-pack can cost hours of time. The listing says pre-assembled, tool-free or full assembly required.

howToChoose.intro: Match slots to your device count.

cards.label: Locked
cards.text: Doors with a lock keep devices secured. The Meteteel, VEVOR and TIOPLY do this.

cards.label: Open rack
cards.text: An open rack is easier to load and ventilate but not locked. The Plugsharge uses it.

howToChoose.note: Most schools should default to locked unless the room itself is locked.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A cart that arrives mostly assembled, with cable management already built in.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Meteteel 20-device cart arrives 95 percent pre-assembled. The Pearington needs full assembly.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need locking doors or 30 plus slots, as on the Meteteel or TIOPLY.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have 16 devices and a locked room. The Hupsjer is a tier cheaper.

faq.a: It is the same line as the 20-device cart, so we kept the larger one.

faq.q: Do these protect against power surges?
faq.a: The VEVOR and Plugsharge list surge protection, and the others vary. Check the specs.
The Plugsharge and TIOPLY list slots that size or larger.

faq.q: Is a locked cart worth it?
faq.a: For shared fleets, yes. The Meteteel and VEVOR lock the doors.
The Meteteel is 95 percent pre-assembled, while the Pearington needs full assembly.

faq.q: Can I roll a full cart?
faq.a: Yes, but only some casters lock, so brake it before loading or unloading.

finalTake: The Meteteel 20-device cart is the best all-round pick for most schools, with locking doors and almost no setup. Take the VEVOR for a smaller lockable fleet, TIOPLY for the largest, and the Hupsjer when cost matters most.
